text:
A: Hello. Can you hear me alright?
B: Yeah, hiya. Darren.
A: Gareth. Nice to meet you.
B: And you. Did you get through that puzzle alright?
A: Yeah, got through it. Couple I wasn't sure about. You?
B: Same. Ran out of time on the last one, to be fair.
A: Whereabouts are you, then?
B: Stourbridge. You sound local-ish.
A: Shirley, Solihull. Grew up in Acocks Green, though.
B: Ah, right. Not far, then.
A: No. What do you do?
B: Gas engineer. Heating firm in Halesowen, mostly boilers. Servicing, repairs, replacements, that sort of thing.
A: Busy this time of year, I'd imagine.
B: Yeah, no, it's been mad. Winter's always the worst, everyone's boiler packs up the first cold week. Had one yesterday, eight years old, heat exchanger gone. People don't get them serviced, they think it's a waste of money, then they're ringing Sunday night with no hot water and two kids in the house. And half the time it's a cheap unit someone's fitted badly to start with, so you're sort of fixing somebody else's job as well.
A: Yeah. We see a bit of that. Different scale.
B: What is it you do?
A: Quantity surveyor. Senior Commercial Manager at a contractor in Birmingham, hospitals and schools mainly. I look after the money side. Cost reports, valuations, subcontractor accounts, you know.
B: Right. So you're the one telling people they're not getting paid what they asked for.
A: Pretty much, yeah. Politely.
B: Ha. I've got a mate does the M&E side on them big jobs, he moans about QSs all the time.
A: They all do. Then they ring me when they want paying early.
B: Do you have much to do with heat pumps on your jobs? Everyone keeps telling me I've got to do the training.
A: Er, yeah, on the new schools mostly. Air source. Spec's all heading that way now, so... I'd do it, if I were you. Work's going there whether anyone likes it or not.
B: Yeah. I know. I just don't trust them yet in a seventies semi with no insulation, you know. You put one in, it's not keeping up, and who's the customer ringing? Me.
A: That's fair.
B: You got kids?
A: Two. Oliver's eleven, Isla's eight. You?
B: Two as well. Ellie's fifteen, Jack's twelve. Wife's Claire.
A: Sorry, say that again?
B: Wife's called Claire.
A: So's mine.
B: Get away.
A: Honestly. Claire. Part-time, in HR.
B: Mine's part-time on reception at a dentist. That's a bit weird, that.
A: Must be the area. Football?
B: Baggies. Always have been.
A: Blues.
B: Oh dear. Well, we'll not fall out over it. Still go?
A: Half-season share with a mate. Don't make as many as I should. Owners don't help.
B: No, we've had our share of that an' all. I get to a few with my brother-in-law, rest is on the radio in the van.
A: Not a bad way to do it. You can turn it off when they're losing.
B: That's about it really.
A: Booked next year's holiday yet? I've done ours already. January's when the deals are.
B: Same caravan park near Tenby, every summer. Booked it the week we got back.
A: Can't beat knowing what you're getting.
B: That's what I keep telling Claire.
A: Which one?
B: Ha. Either, probably.
